honesty.issue: Bearing ring tolerances are recalled from memory ('ISO 492 Normal 的記憶值') and presented in tables as the standard. The OD value is wrong for D = 52 (0/-11 is the 30-50 mm class; 50-80 mm is 0/-13), which shifts every housing number by 2 um. The caveat 'check with the supplier catalogue' is present.

Turn 1 invented a hypothetical axial chain (31 +-0.10 housing, two 6205s) and gave '0.90-1.34 mm' results for it before asking for the real chain. It was labelled as an example, but it is noise for the user.

Turn 5 assumed the 0.5 mm shim sits inside the clamped length (subtracted it) and declared '外圈裝不進去 ... 要改圖' without asking where the shim sits. A shim under the cover flange adds 0.5 mm instead, and Jason said it is probably an assembly adjustment shim. That was a confident redesign advice on an unchecked assumption.
It was transparent that the thermal growth inputs were hand-computed (alpha x L x dT) and only summed by the tool, and that the chart PNG could not be produced.

problems.what: metrology_fit_limits only knows ISO 286 hole/shaft pairs. A bearing seat needs the ISO 492 ring tolerances, which the model then has to recall. Here it recalled the 52 mm OD class wrongly (0/-11 instead of 0/-13 um).
problems.evidence: Assistant: '外徑 52 0/−11 µm'; stackup input {name: 'bearing OD 6205 (0/-11 um)', nominal: '51.9945 mm', tol: '0.0055 mm'}
problems.fix: Add a bearing option to metrology_fit_limits, e.g. fit 'L0/k5' or a 'bearing_class: normal|P6|P5' argument with nominal d/D, that uses tabulated ISO 492 radial-bearing bore and OD deviations and returns the real seat clearance/interference.

problems.what: Housing advice reversed. It said aluminium's larger expansion makes K7 risky, then recommended the looser H7, which runs at +30..+71 um clearance at 70 C (its own numbers). That invites outer-ring creep in a light-alloy housing. Catalogue practice for light alloy is a tighter fit (K7/M7), so his existing K7 was acceptable.
problems.evidence: Turn 1: 'K7 在鋁座上有額外風險：鋁的熱膨脹係數約是鋼的兩倍，溫度升高時座孔脹得比軸承快，配合會鬆動'; turn 2: 'H7（建議）：70°C 時為 +30 ～ +71 µm 間隙 ... 間隙配合可以接受'
problems.fix: See -3. A skill note would catch this.

problems.what: No eng-toolkit skill covers bearing seat fits. Nothing says that fit_limits gives the ISO 286 pair and not the bearing seat, which ring tolerances to combine (with the stackup trick the assistant used), or that light-alloy housings and temperature call for tighter outer-ring fits.
problems.evidence: plugin/skills/eng-toolkit/SKILL.md line 36 only lists 'fit_limits (ISO 286 fits), fit_search, stackup_1d'; no skill mentions bearing or ISO 492
problems.fix: Add a short 'bearing seats' section (eng-toolkit SKILL.md or a new eng-tolerancing skill): 'For a rolling bearing seat, fit_limits gives the shaft/housing limits only; combine them with the ring tolerance via stackup_1d (or the bearing option, once added); rotating inner ring -> k5/k6/m5 by load; stationary outer ring -> H7 in steel/cast iron, K7/M7 in aluminium or when the housing runs hot; compute the thermal change of the fit.'

problems.what: Charting: the assistant never loaded plot_bar or eng-plot-results. It hand-wrote an SVG with the Write tool, then tried matplotlib and System.Drawing scripts. The toolkit's plot tools also produce SVG only, so the user's PNG/PDF request could not be met through the toolkit either.
problems.evidence: Turn 2 tools: Write fit_compare.svg, Edit (axis relabel). Turn 3/4: make_fit_chart.py, make_fit_chart.ps1, blocked PowerShell runs. eng-plot-results SKILL.md: 'Not covered: ... PNG/PDF'
problems.fix: eng-toolkit SKILL.md: 'Charts: always use plot_bar/plot_xy (eng-plot-results); never hand-write SVG.' Tool side: add formats 'svg,png,pdf' to plot_xy/plot_bar/plot_panels (the drawing tool already rasterises with PDFium), and add a floating-range bar mode (min..max per category) for fit/tolerance comparisons.

problems.what: The outer-ring chain treats the 0.5 mm shim as part of the clamped length without asking where it sits. It then concluded the outer ring cannot be assembled and that the drawing must change (15.3 -> 15.1, remove the shim).
problems.evidence: Turn 5 stackup chain {gasket 0.5 mm, direction '-'} -> nominal -0.14; '加了 0.5 墊片，外圈裝不進去 ... 會頂壞'. Turn 6 person: '墊片 ... 可能是組裝時用來調的'; assistant still: '外圈：要改圖'
problems.fix: No toolkit change. A skill note on stack-ups ('ask where every spacer/shim sits and whether it is selected at assembly before declaring interference') would help.

what_worked: It built the real bearing seats with metrology_stackup_1d (shaft limits from fit_limits against the ring tolerance) and explained that the H7/k5 table value is not the bearing seat. This is exactly the trap the truth names.
The stack-up with the asymmetric tolerances re-centred, worst case and Monte Carlo against 0.1/0.5 gives correct numbers and a clear 'NOT OK' with the probability above the limit.
It proposed a single-dimension fix with the margin stated honestly, and checked the fix with the same tool.
It confirmed the circlip tolerance reading, and recovered quickly when corrected on the groove location and the all-steel chain.
Its final summary table answered every question Jason asked in turn 6.
